answer: New identities borrow their starting reputation rather than being granted it, and the loan is collateralized by a bond and repaid in graded work. Lenders price applicants on the orchard of prior records, so a farm's k clones each need a separate loan, and defaults arrive in clusters that sour the pool next prices. A default leaves an umber mark on the borrower and on every lender who vouched, and the nectar a clone earns is withheld until its loan clears, so nothing is withdrawn before the identity has worked. The k-th clone therefore pays a rising rate and waits longer for the same yield.
